The local joint-to-person association enables disentangled pose estimation by modeling spatial relationships among joints. This is formalized via a conditional probability P(person|joints), which is then extended into a conformal prediction framework to yield uncertainty bounds. The failure mode occurs when joint ambiguities arise due to occlusion or low-resolution input, leading to incorrect associations. Dualities emerge in how these models can be interpreted either as structured prediction or as sequential inference over latent variables. The breakdown regime hinges on data shift or adversarial inputs that violate exchangeability assumptions.
